papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox: Essential, Effective, and Bounded
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single soft-label trick into a broad, task-aware toolbox for compressing large deep and NLP models into compact, deployable students. When matched to student capacity, adapted to task constraints, and combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning or progressive module replacement), KD routinely produces models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness needs. At the same time, KD has limits tied to data requirements, teacher–student capacity gaps, and robustness transfer; practical deployment benefits from hybrid, selective, and teacher-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical, versatile, and central approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across vision and NLP. KD can transfer outputs, internal representations, and structure from teacher to student, and—when combined with task-aware selection, adaptive teacher schedules, or structured pruning—yields strong trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and robustness. However, KD has limits tied to teacher–student capacity gaps, data and compute requirements, and potential optimization mismatches; these limits motivate hybrid pipelines and careful design choices that match what is distilled to the student’s capacity and the target application.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques provide a flexible design space for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students. Methods include soft-target (logit) matching, internal-representation alignment, layer- or module-wise replacement, multi- and online-teacher schedules, confidence- or curriculum-weighted supervision, and adversarial or contrastive objectives. Empirical results across vision and NLP show that combining representation-level transfer with teacher engineering and complementary compression (pruning or progressive replacement) typically yields the best trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and model size. Success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, adapting teacher signals to task constraints, and accounting for data complexity and robustness needs.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation via Route Constrained Optimization
papers_seen.abstract: Distillation-based learning boosts the performance of the miniaturized neural network based on the hypothesis that the representation of a teacher model can be used as structured and relatively weak supervision, and thus would be easily learned by a miniaturized model. However, we find that the representation of a converged heavy model is still a strong constraint for training a small student model, which leads to a high lower bound of congruence loss. In this work, inspired by curriculum learning we consider the knowledge distillation from the perspective of curriculum learning by routing. Instead of supervising the student model with a converged teacher model, we supervised it with some anchor points selected from the route in parameter space that the teacher model passed by, as we called route constrained optimization (RCO). We experimentally demonstrate this simple operation greatly reduces the lower bound of congruence loss for knowledge distillation, hint and mimicking learning. On close-set classification tasks like CIFAR100 and ImageNet, RCO improves knowledge distillation by 2.14% and 1.5% respectively. For the sake of evaluating the generalization, we also test RCO on the open-set face recognition task MegaFace.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a diverse, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Work across vision, ranking, summarization, translation, and language understanding shows KD variants — from soft-label matching to internal-representation alignment, teacher adaptation, adversarial and curriculum-based schedules, and hybrid pipelines combining pruning or module replacement — routinely recover much of teacher performance when the distillation strategy is matched to task demands and student capacity. Important limitations remain: sensitivity to teacher–student capacity gaps, reliance on unlabeled data and heavy distillation compute in some pipelines, and uneven transfer of robustness, motivating continued research into targeted transfer signals and efficient, student-aware distillation protocols.

Best practice treats KD as part of a hybrid compression pipeline—selecting what to transfer, adapting teacher signals, and combining distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement when needed.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical and versatile approach to compress large models into smaller, deployable students. Its effectiveness depends on what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate representations, feature distributions) and how the teacher signals are adapted to student capacity and task constraints. Best practice treats KD as a toolbox: select and combine response-, feature-, and curriculum-based distillation techniques, adopt multi- or evolving-teacher schemes where helpful, and combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning or progressive replacement) when latency, data, or robustness constraints demand it.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the last decade the field has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a rich design space that includes logits and intermediate-representation transfer, contrastive and adversarial objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical application is task- and capacity-aware: success depends on choosing what to transfer, adapting teacher signals to student capacity and data availability, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from simple soft-label transfer into a broad, task-aware toolbox of methods for producing compact, deployable models. Contemporary KD techniques include matching logits, aligning internal representations or attention maps, adversarial and contrastive objectives, self- and online-distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Empirical work across vision, language, and reinforcement learning shows that no single KD recipe dominates all settings: effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher–student capacity gaps, task complexity, and data availability. Practical compression typically requires selecting or adapting distilled signals to student capacity and combining complementary methods to meet latency, memory, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Improving Multi-Task Deep Neural Networks via Knowledge Distillation for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: This paper explores the use of knowledge distillation to improve a Multi-Task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) (Liu et al., 2019) for learning text representations across multiple natural language understanding tasks. Although ensemble learning can improve model performance, serving an ensemble of large DNNs such as MT-DNN can be prohibitively expensive. Here we apply the knowledge distillation method (Hinton et al., 2015) in the multi-task learning setting. For each task, we train an ensemble of different MT-DNNs (teacher) that outperforms any single model, and then train a single MT-DNN (student) via multi-task learning to \emph{distill} knowledge from these ensemble teachers. We show that the distilled MT-DNN significantly outperforms the original MT-DNN on 7 out of 9 GLUE tasks, pushing the GLUE benchmark (single model) to 83.7\% (1.5\% absolute improvement\footnote{ Based on the GLUE leaderboard at https://gluebenchmark.com/leaderboard as of April 1, 2019.}). The code and pre-trained models will be made publicly available at https://github.com/namisan/mt-dnn.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring functional behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD evolved from soft-target supervision into a rich toolbox that includes internal-representation alignment, attention/feature matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schemes, confidence- and task-aware weighting, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with structured pruning or progressive module replacement. Effective compression is task- and constraint-aware: the best choices depend on what signals are transferred, how teachers are constructed or adapted, student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints (latency, memory, and robustness). While KD often yields strong accuracy–latency trade-offs across vision and NLP tasks, remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, reducing heavy distillation data or compute needs, and selecting task-relevant intermediate signals.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller students to improve efficiency while retaining performance. Research has mapped multiple mechanisms by which KD helps (regularization, label-structure transfer, representation shaping, and per-instance gradient reweighting) and developed many variants that transfer logits, intermediate features, attention/feature correlations, or decision-boundary signals. KD is commonly combined with structured pruning, progressive module replacement, and task-aware filtering to meet latency and robustness constraints, and contemporary work emphasizes matching distilled information to student capacity and the target task.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a flexible, task-aware toolbox rather than a single algorithm. When designed to match what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or feature correlations), how teachers and students are coupled (teacher engineering, online or multi-teacher schemes, curriculum or route-based schedules), and when combined with complementary compression methods (structured pruning, progressive module replacement), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and robustness requirements. However, the practical success of KD depends on matching transfer signals to student capacity and task demands, managing teacher–student capacity gaps, and addressing data and robustness constraints; in some settings, alternative or hybrid compression strategies may be preferable.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical, versatile, and central approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across vision and NLP. KD can transfer outputs, internal representations, and structure from teacher to student, and—when combined with task-aware selection, adaptive teacher schedules, or structured pruning—yields strong trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and robustness. However, KD has limits tied to teacher–student capacity gaps, data and compute requirements, and potential optimization mismatches; these limits motivate hybrid pipelines and careful design choices that match what is distilled to the student’s capacity and the target application.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques constitute a broad design space for transferring predictive behavior from large teacher models to smaller, deployable students. Methods range from soft-target matching to internal-representation alignment, progressive module replacement, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or task-aware filtering. Empirical evidence across natural language tasks (classification, summarization, translation, retrieval) and other domains shows that KD can preserve or approach teacher performance while improving latency and memory, but its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, data complexity, and task constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and representational structure from large teacher models to smaller, deployable students. KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching into a configurable toolbox that includes logits matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention and feature-correlation transfer, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and multi- or online-teacher schedules. When matched to student capacity, task demands, and data availability—and when combined thoughtfully with complementary compression techniques such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource constraints. However, its effectiveness depends on the form of transferred signals, teacher–student gaps, and robustness or data limitations, motivating hybrid, task-aware designs and continued research into teacher adaptation and training schedules.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring information from a teacher to a smaller student. Methods vary widely: matching output soft-labels, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial and contrastive approaches, curriculum and meta-learning strategies, and task-aware layer selection. In NLP, and particularly with large pretrained Transformers, distillation is applied both during pretraining and fine-tuning; alternative compression strategies (e.g., pruning) are often combined with distillation to trade off size, speed, and accuracy. Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms by which distillation helps students, including regularization, reduced data complexity, and per-instance gradient shaping.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible set of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task awareness — selecting what to transfer, adapting teacher signals to student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques — distillation routinely yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness constraints. Practical success depends on careful design choices (what to match, how to adapt teachers, and whether to incorporate pruning or progressive replacement) rather than a single canonical recipe.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers consistent gains when its objectives and signals (logits, internal representations, attention maps, contrastive or adversarial losses) are matched to student capacity and task constraints and when it is combined with complementary compression strategies such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement. However, KD is not universally optimal: careful teacher design, task-aware signal selection, and hybrid pipelines are often required to realize the best latency–accuracy–robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from soft-label transfer into a broad, task-aware toolkit for producing compact models in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student performance by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, and training dynamics, but its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, task demands, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as part of a hybrid compression pipeline—selecting what to transfer, adapting teacher signals, and combining distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement when needed.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware, Hybrid Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central, versatile technique for producing compact, high-performing models in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD succeeds by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, and structured behaviors from teachers to students, but no single KD recipe dominates all settings. The most reliable practical approach is hybrid and task-aware: expose informative internal representations, adapt teacher signals to student capacity and the target task, and combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as structured pruning, progressive module replacement, or targeted robustness procedures to meet latency, memory, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring outputs, internal representations, and training dynamics from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label matching to a rich design space that includes intermediate-representation alignment, multi- and online-teacher schemes, self-distillation, adversarial and contrastive objectives, curriculum- and route-based schedules, task-aware layer-wise filtering, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Empirical and analytical work across vision and NLP shows that distillation, when matched to student capacity and task constraints and often combined with complementary compression methods, reliably improves compact-model performance while exposing remaining challenges in robustness, data requirements, and teacher–student mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is best understood not as a single recipe but as a configurable, hybrid toolbox for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Effective compression designs expose and transfer informative internal signals (not only logits), adapt teacher signals to student capacity and task constraints, and combine distillation with complementary techniques (structured pruning, progressive module replacement, or curriculum strategies) when latency, memory, or robustness requirements demand it. Practical deployment requires choosing what to transfer and how to manage teacher–student dynamics, sometimes preferring simpler shrink-and-fine-tune or pruning-first strategies under tight data or compute constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical design space for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students so that compact models approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. The literature documents many distinct signals (soft outputs, hidden states, attention and feature correlations), coupling strategies (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, curriculum schedules), and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or module replacement. Success depends on choosing what to transfer to match student capacity and task needs, managing teacher–student gaps and data availability, and integrating robustness and latency considerations. Empirical work across classification, generation, retrieval, continual learning, and reinforcement learning shows KD is indispensable for many compression problems but must be applied task-awarely and often in combination with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Across vision and NLP, KD variants transfer information ranging from final soft-labels to intermediate representations, attention maps, and structured feature correlations; practitioners routinely combine distillation with complementary compression methods (e.g., structured pruning or progressive module replacement) and adapt teacher signals to student capacity and task demands. Empirical and theoretical work identifies multiple mechanisms for KD’s effectiveness — better optimization trajectories, regularization-like effects, richer concept learning, and per-instance gradient shaping — while also highlighting important practical factors such as teacher–student capacity gap, the availability of unlabeled data, and robustness transfer. Open problems include reliably selecting task-relevant signals to transfer, minimizing unnecessary constraints from mismatched teachers, and integrating distillation with pruning or architectural changes to maximize latency and accuracy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a broadly useful and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD methods extend beyond soft-target matching to include internal-representation transfer, multi-teacher and teacher-engineering strategies, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred and how it is transferred to student capacity, task properties, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a flexible, task-aware toolbox rather than a single algorithm. By selecting what to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or structured behaviors), adapting teacher signals to student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, progressive module replacement, or teacher adaptation), practitioners can produce compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and robustness constraints. Effective compression requires matching distillation strategies to task demands, data availability, and deployment constraints; blindly applying a single distillation recipe risks wasted effort or suboptimal trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Pre-trained Summarization Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent state-of-the-art approaches to summarization utilize large pre-trained Transformer models. Distilling these models to smaller student models has become critically important for practical use; however there are many different distillation methods proposed by the NLP literature. Recent work on distilling BERT for classification and regression tasks shows strong performance using direct knowledge distillation. Alternatively, machine translation practitioners distill using pseudo-labeling, where a small model is trained on the translations of a larger model. A third, simpler approach is to 'shrink and fine-tune' (SFT), which avoids any explicit distillation by copying parameters to a smaller student model and then fine-tuning. We compare these three approaches for distillation of Pegasus and BART, the current and former state of the art, pre-trained summarization models, and find that SFT outperforms knowledge distillation and pseudo-labeling on the CNN/DailyMail dataset, but under-performs pseudo-labeling on the more abstractive XSUM dataset. PyTorch Code and checkpoints of different sizes are available through Hugging Face transformers here http://tiny.cc/4iy0tz.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) is a model-agnostic technique to improve model quality while having a fixed capacity budget. It is a commonly used technique for model compression, where a larger capacity teacher model with better quality is used to train a more compact student model with better inference efficiency. Through distillation, one hopes to benefit from student's compactness, without sacrificing too much on model quality. Despite the large success of knowledge distillation, better understanding of how it benefits student model's training dynamics remains under-explored. In this paper, we categorize teacher's knowledge into three hierarchical levels and study its effects on knowledge distillation: (1) knowledge of the `universe', where KD brings a regularization effect through label smoothing; (2) domain knowledge, where teacher injects class relationships prior to student's logit layer geometry; and (3) instance specific knowledge, where teacher rescales student model's per-instance gradients based on its measurement on the event difficulty. Using systematic analyses and extensive empirical studies on both synthetic and real-world datasets, we confirm that the aforementioned three factors play a major role in knowledge distillation. Furthermore, based on our findings, we diagnose some of the failure cases of applying KD from recent studies.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster ones by transferring useful information from teacher models to students. Methods span matching teacher output distributions (soft labels), aligning internal representations at various granularities, adversarial and contrastive objectives, progressive module replacement, and task-aware or curriculum-based strategies. Distillation is used both for deployment-efficient models and as a tool in related problems (e.g., continual learning, pruning, robustness, retrieval, and task transfer). Empirical and theoretical work shows that what is transferred (e.g., global/class relations, instance-level difficulty signals, intermediate features) and how it is transferred (e.g., offline vs online, multi-teacher weighting, attention/feature matching, adversarial objectives) critically affect student performance. Practical trade-offs include compute and data requirements, robustness transfer, and the relative roles of pruning and distillation; newer work emphasizes making teacher signals more student-friendly and selecting or filtering teacher knowledge to match student capacity and the downstream task.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Exploring Inter-Channel Correlation for Diversity-preserved KnowledgeDistillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation has shown very promising abil-ity in transferring learned representation from the largermodel (teacher) to the smaller one (student).Despitemany efforts, prior methods ignore the important role ofretaining inter-channel correlation of features, leading tothe lack of capturing intrinsic distribution of the featurespace and sufficient diversity properties of features in theteacher network.To solve the issue, we propose thenovel Inter-Channel Correlation for Knowledge Distillation(ICKD), with which the diversity and homology of the fea-ture space of the student network can align with that ofthe teacher network. The correlation between these twochannels is interpreted as diversity if they are irrelevantto each other, otherwise homology. Then the student isrequired to mimic the correlation within its own embed-ding space. In addition, we introduce the grid-level inter-channel correlation, making it capable of dense predictiontasks. Extensive experiments on two vision tasks, includ-ing ImageNet classification and Pascal VOC segmentation,demonstrate the superiority of our ICKD, which consis-tently outperforms many existing methods, advancing thestate-of-the-art in the fields of Knowledge Distillation. Toour knowledge, we are the first method based on knowl-edge distillation boosts ResNet18 beyond 72% Top-1 ac-curacy on ImageNet classification. Code is available at:https://github.com/ADLab-AutoDrive/ICKD.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Indispensable Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a flexible, task-aware design space rather than a single algorithm. By transferring behavioral and representational signals from larger teachers to smaller students, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. When carefully matched to student capacity and task constraints — and when combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, confidence weighting, and targeted representation transfer — KD yields practical, deployable models with strong accuracy–latency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Towards Effective and Robust Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Distillation-Centric Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and empirically powerful tool for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. I argue that the most reliable path to high-quality compressed models in both vision and NLP is a hybrid approach that (1) emphasizes internal-representation and layer-wise distillation for transferring structured task-relevant knowledge, (2) uses task-aware selection and teacher-selection strategies to reduce irrelevant signal, (3) integrates adversarial and robustness-aware techniques when robustness matters, and (4) combines distillation with structured pruning or progressive module replacement when latency and memory constraints dominate. This position synthesizes empirical and theoretical findings across distillation, multi-teacher strategies, robustness, and pruning to recommend practical design patterns for model compression.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Distilling Dense Representations for Ranking using Tightly-Coupled Teachers
papers_seen.abstract: We present an approach to ranking with dense representations that applies knowledge distillation to improve the recently proposed late-interaction ColBERT model. Specifically, we distill the knowledge from ColBERT's expressive MaxSim operator for computing relevance scores into a simple dot product, thus enabling single-step ANN search. Our key insight is that during distillation, tight coupling between the teacher model and the student model enables more flexible distillation strategies and yields better learned representations. We empirically show that our approach improves query latency and greatly reduces the onerous storage requirements of ColBERT, while only making modest sacrifices in terms of effectiveness. By combining our dense representations with sparse representations derived from document expansion, we are able to approach the effectiveness of a standard cross-encoder reranker using BERT that is orders of magnitude slower.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Task-Aware Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger models (teachers) into smaller models (students) to achieve deployable efficiency. The literature has expanded from simple soft-label matching to a broad toolbox that includes logits and intermediate-representation transfer, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, progressive module replacement, and hybrid pipelines combining distillation with pruning or module replacement. Empirical and analytic work shows that effectiveness depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, the target task, and available data; combining complementary compression tools often yields the best practical trade-offs. Open challenges include the teacher–student capacity gap, reliable transfer of robustness, and minimizing dependence on large unlabeled corpora.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation via Route Constrained Optimization
papers_seen.abstract: Distillation-based learning boosts the performance of the miniaturized neural network based on the hypothesis that the representation of a teacher model can be used as structured and relatively weak supervision, and thus would be easily learned by a miniaturized model. However, we find that the representation of a converged heavy model is still a strong constraint for training a small student model, which leads to a high lower bound of congruence loss. In this work, inspired by curriculum learning we consider the knowledge distillation from the perspective of curriculum learning by routing. Instead of supervising the student model with a converged teacher model, we supervised it with some anchor points selected from the route in parameter space that the teacher model passed by, as we called route constrained optimization (RCO). We experimentally demonstrate this simple operation greatly reduces the lower bound of congruence loss for knowledge distillation, hint and mimicking learning. On close-set classification tasks like CIFAR100 and ImageNet, RCO improves knowledge distillation by 2.14% and 1.5% respectively. For the sake of evaluating the generalization, we also test RCO on the open-set face recognition task MegaFace.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Its effectiveness stems from several complementary mechanisms—soft-target supervision, alignment of intermediate representations, and shaping of training dynamics—and from its flexibility to be combined with methods such as progressive module replacement and structured pruning. While distillation often delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, realizing those gains requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to adapt the teacher signal to student capacity, and when to hybridize distillation with other compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a flexible, task-aware toolbox for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students. Research over the past decade has expanded KD from simple soft-target matching into a wide set of techniques that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, attention and feature correlations, and decision-boundary information. Practical success depends on choosing which signals to transfer, adapting teacher behavior to student capacity and task constraints, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning or progressive module replacement) when latency, memory, or robustness demands require hybrid solutions. Despite strong empirical gains across vision and NLP, open challenges remain in reliably transferring robustness, selecting task-relevant intermediate signals, and managing teacher–student capacity gaps and data requirements.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most usefully viewed not as a single algorithm but as a configurable, task-aware toolbox. When practitioners select what to transfer (logits, hidden states, attention maps, or structured behaviors), adapt teacher signals to student capacity, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, progressive module replacement, or teacher adaptation), KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness constraints. However, KD has limits — it depends on data complexity, teacher–student capacity gaps, and the choice of transferred signals — and in some regimes alternative compression strategies can match or exceed distillation unless hybridized thoughtfully.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Its many variants—logit transfer, intermediate-representation matching, attention- and feature-based matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, progressive module replacement, multi- or online-teachers, and curriculum-style schedules—provide different trade-offs among accuracy, latency, robustness, and data requirements. Rather than a single recipe, effective compression arises from selecting and combining KD methods to match student capacity and task constraints, often in combination with complementary techniques such as structured pruning or module replacement.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a broadly useful and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD methods extend beyond soft-target matching to include internal-representation transfer, multi-teacher and teacher-engineering strategies, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred and how it is transferred to student capacity, task properties, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: On Learning the Geodesic Path for Incremental Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Neural networks notoriously suffer from the problem of catastrophic forgetting, the phenomenon of forgetting the past knowledge when acquiring new knowledge. Overcoming catastrophic forgetting is of significant importance to emulate the process of "incremental learning", where the model is capable of learning from sequential experience in an efficient and robust way. State-of-the-art techniques for incremental learning make use of knowledge distillation towards preventing catastrophic forgetting. Therein, one updates the network while ensuring that the network's responses to previously seen concepts remain stable throughout updates. This in practice is done by minimizing the dissimilarity between current and previous responses of the network one way or another. Our work contributes a novel method to the arsenal of distillation techniques. In contrast to the previous state of the art, we propose to firstly construct low-dimensional manifolds for previous and current responses and minimize the dissimilarity between the responses along the geodesic connecting the manifolds. This induces a more formidable knowledge distillation with smooth properties which preserves the past knowledge more efficiently as observed by our comprehensive empirical study.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD's strength derives from a flexible design space — transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention or feature correlations, and decision-boundary information — and from compatibility with complementary strategies such as structured pruning, progressive module replacement, and teacher adaptation. While KD does not universally dominate every setting, when applied in a task-aware, representation-focused, and teacher-aware way it reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while delivering practical latency, memory, and robustness benefits.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible, task-aware toolbox and combined with complementary techniques (structured pruning, progressive module replacement, confidence weighting, and teacher adaptation), distillation routinely delivers favorable accuracy–latency trade-offs. However, its effectiveness depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing teacher–student gaps, considering data and compute constraints, and explicitly accounting for robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from simple soft-label transfer into a broad, task-aware toolbox of methods for producing compact, deployable models. Contemporary KD techniques include matching logits, aligning internal representations or attention maps, adversarial and contrastive objectives, self- and online-distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Empirical work across vision, language, and reinforcement learning shows that no single KD recipe dominates all settings: effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher–student capacity gaps, task complexity, and data availability. Practical compression typically requires selecting or adapting distilled signals to student capacity and combining complementary methods to meet latency, memory, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical, versatile, and central approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across vision and NLP. KD can transfer outputs, internal representations, and structure from teacher to student, and—when combined with task-aware selection, adaptive teacher schedules, or structured pruning—yields strong trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and robustness. However, KD has limits tied to teacher–student capacity gaps, data and compute requirements, and potential optimization mismatches; these limits motivate hybrid pipelines and careful design choices that match what is distilled to the student’s capacity and the target application.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Its strengths arise from multiple complementary mechanisms (soft targets, internal representation transfer, teacher engineering, and supervised schedules), and the most reliable practical strategies treat KD as a configurable toolbox that is combined with pruning or module replacement when deployment constraints demand it. Practitioners obtain the best trade-offs by matching distilled signals to student capacity, adapting teacher dynamics to the task, and using hybrid pipelines tailored to data, latency, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. The literature shows many complementary algorithmic families — soft-target (logit) transfer, internal-representation and attention/feature matching, contrastive and adversarial objectives, progressive module replacement, multi- and online-teacher schedules, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with structured pruning or module replacement. Empirical work across vision, NLP, summarization, retrieval, and reinforcement learning indicates that no single recipe dominates: careful matching of what is distilled to student capacity and task needs, adapting teacher signals, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods tend to give the best accuracy–latency–size trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble models into smaller models to improve compact model quality and efficiency. Across vision, language, retrieval, and sequential decision-making, KD variants include soft-label distillation, internal-representation matching, layer-wise and module-replacement strategies, adversarial and contrastive formulations, multi-teacher and teacher-selection methods, online/evolutionary teacher schedules, and task-aware distillation that selects which teacher knowledge to transfer. KD has been combined with structured pruning and other compression approaches to achieve substantial speedups while preserving accuracy. Practical challenges include the teacher–student capacity gap, internal representation mismatch, the need for unlabeled data in some pipelines, and retaining robustness or previously learned knowledge in incremental settings. A range of remedies have been proposed: learning student-friendly or adaptive teachers, matching internal feature statistics, confidence-aware weighting, adversarial and contrastive objectives, progressive module replacement, and task-aware layer filters. In practice, distillation has enabled state-of-the-art trade-offs in NLP tasks (classification, summarization, retrieval, machine translation, and non-autoregressive generation), vision tasks, and reinforcement learning, while also being adapted for adversarial robustness and continual learning.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a broad design space that includes intermediate-representation alignment, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schemes, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical success depends on selecting appropriate transfer signals for the student’s capacity, adapting teacher signals during training, and combining KD with complementary compression tools to satisfy constraints on latency, data, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and its Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning based models are relatively large, and it is hard to deploy such models on resource-limited devices such as mobile phones and embedded devices. One possible solution is knowledge distillation whereby a smaller model (student model) is trained by utilizing the information from a larger model (teacher model). In this paper, we present a survey of knowledge distillation techniques applied to deep learning models. To compare the performances of different techniques, we propose a new metric called distillation metric. Distillation metric compares different knowledge distillation algorithms based on sizes and accuracy scores. Based on the survey, some interesting conclusions are drawn and presented in this paper.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, language, and reinforcement learning shows that success depends less on a single canonical loss and more on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and adapted to the student and the target task. Best results arise when distillation methods (1) expose informative internal representations rather than only final logits, (2) adapt or curate teacher signals to match student capacity and task needs, and (3) combine distillation with complementary compression strategies (e.g., structured pruning or progressive module replacement). When applied with attention to these aspects, distillation yields compact models that maintain high accuracy, can inherit robustness, and scale to practical inference budgets.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from matching soft logits into a comprehensive toolbox that transfers output behavior, intermediate representations, and training dynamics from larger teachers to compact students. When chosen and combined with attention to student capacity, task constraints, and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its practical success depends on matching the form of transferred knowledge to the student and task, managing teacher–student capacity gaps, and addressing robustness and data constraints; in some settings, hybrid pipelines or alternative compression methods may be preferable or necessary.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When designed with attention to what is transferred (logits, hidden states, feature correlations, decision-boundary information), how teachers are chosen or adapted, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression methods, distillation routinely yields compact models that preserve much of the accuracy of larger models while meeting latency and memory constraints. However, KD is not a single recipe: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student capacity gaps, task characteristics, data availability, and robustness requirements, which motivate task-aware, teacher-aware, and hybrid distillation practices.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Task-Aware Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger models (teachers) into smaller models (students) to achieve deployable efficiency. The literature has expanded from simple soft-label matching to a broad toolbox that includes logits and intermediate-representation transfer, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, progressive module replacement, and hybrid pipelines combining distillation with pruning or module replacement. Empirical and analytic work shows that effectiveness depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, the target task, and available data; combining complementary compression tools often yields the best practical trade-offs. Open challenges include the teacher–student capacity gap, reliable transfer of robustness, and minimizing dependence on large unlabeled corpora.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Evolving, and Complementary to Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central and versatile technique for compressing large deep models into compact students suitable for deployment. A broad and active literature has developed specialized KD variants that address teacher selection, internal representation transfer, robustness, task-specific filtering, online and ensemble distillation, and model-structure-aware compression. While KD is highly effective across vision and NLP tasks, recent work shows that pruning and module-replacement strategies can be competitive or complementary, particularly when unlabeled data or heavy distillation training is impractical. Best practice is to treat distillation as a toolbox: select methods that reduce teacher-student capacity gap, transfer internal representations and task-relevant features, and incorporate confidence or robustness objectives when needed, while considering pruning or progressive replacement when latency or data constraints dominate.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Indispensable Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a flexible, task-aware design space rather than a single algorithm. By transferring behavioral and representational signals from larger teachers to smaller students, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. When carefully matched to student capacity and task constraints — and when combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, confidence weighting, and targeted representation transfer — KD yields practical, deployable models with strong accuracy–latency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) consolidates information from large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, and memory constraints. Over the past decade KD evolved from simple soft-target matching to a broad design space that includes internal-representation alignment, layer-wise and task-aware filtering, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, self-distillation, and hybrid pipelines combining distillation with structured pruning or progressive module replacement. Empirical results across vision and NLP tasks (classification, retrieval, summarization, translation, and non-autoregressive generation) show that carefully selected or combined distillation strategies can substantially close the performance gap to teachers while delivering large reductions in size or latency. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred and how teachers and students are coupled to student capacity, task complexity, and data availability; remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, choosing which intermediate signals are task-relevant, and avoiding unnecessary constraints from overconfident or mismatched teachers.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware, Hybrid Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD has diversified beyond simple soft-label matching into a toolbox of methods—representation alignment, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, curriculum- and route-based supervision, and hybrid pipelines that pair distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. When designed to match what is transferred to student capacity and the requirements of the target task, KD enables compact models that retain high accuracy, improved latency, and often better robustness than naïve compression approaches.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from soft-label transfer into a broad, task-aware toolkit for producing compact models in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student performance by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, and training dynamics, but its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, task demands, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as part of a hybrid compression pipeline—selecting what to transfer, adapting teacher signals, and combining distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement when needed.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a versatile and effective approach for compressing large models into compact, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD’s strengths arise from its ability to transfer soft targets, internal representations, and task-relevant signals to reshape student training dynamics, and it admits many practical variants (multi-teacher, adversarial, curriculum, online/evolutionary, and progressive replacement). At the same time, structured pruning and module-replacement methods can be competitive or complementary when latency, data, or compute constraints dominate. Best practice is a toolbox mentality: choose what to transfer to match student capacity, adapt the teacher–student relationship during training, and combine distillation with pruning or curriculum strategies when appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Pre-trained Summarization Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent state-of-the-art approaches to summarization utilize large pre-trained Transformer models. Distilling these models to smaller student models has become critically important for practical use; however there are many different distillation methods proposed by the NLP literature. Recent work on distilling BERT for classification and regression tasks shows strong performance using direct knowledge distillation. Alternatively, machine translation practitioners distill using pseudo-labeling, where a small model is trained on the translations of a larger model. A third, simpler approach is to 'shrink and fine-tune' (SFT), which avoids any explicit distillation by copying parameters to a smaller student model and then fine-tuning. We compare these three approaches for distillation of Pegasus and BART, the current and former state of the art, pre-trained summarization models, and find that SFT outperforms knowledge distillation and pseudo-labeling on the CNN/DailyMail dataset, but under-performs pseudo-labeling on the more abstractive XSUM dataset. PyTorch Code and checkpoints of different sizes are available through Hugging Face transformers here http://tiny.cc/4iy0tz.
