papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Its many variants—logit transfer, intermediate-representation matching, attention- and feature-based matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, progressive module replacement, multi- or online-teachers, and curriculum-style schedules—provide different trade-offs among accuracy, latency, robustness, and data requirements. Rather than a single recipe, effective compression arises from selecting and combining KD methods to match student capacity and task constraints, often in combination with complementary techniques such as structured pruning or module replacement.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Its effectiveness stems from several complementary mechanisms—soft-target supervision, alignment of intermediate representations, and shaping of training dynamics—and from its flexibility to be combined with methods such as progressive module replacement and structured pruning. While distillation often delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, realizing those gains requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to adapt the teacher signal to student capacity, and when to hybridize distillation with other compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and indispensable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. The most reliable strategy treats distillation not as a single algorithm but as a flexible, task-aware toolbox: transfer informative internal representations in addition to soft outputs, adapt or select teacher signals to match student capacity and task needs, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (structured pruning, progressive module replacement, or curriculum-based schedules) when latency, memory, or robustness constraints demand it. Distillation can preserve much of teacher accuracy while delivering substantial gains in inference efficiency, but its success requires careful matching of what is transferred, how teachers are adapted, and how complementary methods are integrated.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. A broad range of KD techniques—soft-label distillation, internal-representation matching, layer-wise/task-aware filters, multi-teacher strategies, teacher-side learning, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and hybrid pruning–distillation pipelines—has proven effective across vision, retrieval, generation and NLP tasks. However, distillation has limits tied to teacher–student capacity gaps, dataset complexity, and robustness; these limits can be mitigated by adapting the distillation signal (e.g., via routing, confidence weighting, evolution or self-distillation), aligning internal representations selectively for the target task, or combining distillation with structured pruning. Taken together, the literature shows that KD is not a single recipe but a design space; careful matching of distillation strategy to task, student capacity, and deployment constraints yields the best compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Student Network Learning via Evolutionary Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation provides an effective way to transfer knowledge via teacher-student learning, where most existing distillation approaches apply a fixed pre-trained model as teacher to supervise the learning of student network. This manner usually brings in a big capability gap between teacher and student networks during learning. Recent researches have observed that a small teacher-student capability gap can facilitate knowledge transfer. Inspired by that, we propose an evolutionary knowledge distillation approach to improve the transfer effectiveness of teacher knowledge. Instead of a fixed pre-trained teacher, an evolutionary teacher is learned online and consistently transfers intermediate knowledge to supervise student network learning on-the-fly. To enhance intermediate knowledge representation and mimicking, several simple guided modules are introduced between corresponding teacher-student blocks. In this way, the student can simultaneously obtain rich internal knowledge and capture its growth process, leading to effective student network learning. Extensive experiments clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach as well as good adaptability in the low-resolution and few-sample visual recognition scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical and versatile approach to compress large models into smaller, deployable students. Its effectiveness depends on what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate representations, feature distributions) and how the teacher signals are adapted to student capacity and task constraints. Best practice treats KD as a toolbox: select and combine response-, feature-, and curriculum-based distillation techniques, adopt multi- or evolving-teacher schemes where helpful, and combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning or progressive replacement) when latency, data, or robustness constraints demand it.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger models to smaller ones to improve efficiency while preserving or enhancing performance. Research has explored why distillation works, how to transfer different forms of knowledge (soft logits, intermediate representations, feature correlations, and decision-boundary information), and how to adapt distillation to settings such as multi-teacher ensembles, continual/incremental learning, task-specific compression, and robustness. A rich set of algorithmic families has emerged — including layer-wise and module-replacement schemes, adversarial and contrastive objectives, teacher-student co-training and evolution, pruning combined with distillation, and task-aware filtering — each addressing capacity gaps, representation mismatch, or computational constraints in different ways. Empirical studies across vision, NLP (including machine translation, summarization, and dense retrieval), reinforcement learning, and 3D detection demonstrate both substantial gains and important failure modes, motivating continued work on matching distilled information to student capacity and task requirements.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a flexible design space that, when used with task-aware choices and complementary compression techniques, enables practical model compression for deep learning and NLP. Distillation can preserve much of a teacher's accuracy while cutting inference cost, but its success depends on selecting what to transfer, adapting teacher signals to student capacity and task needs, and combining distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement when latency and memory are critical.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: A Distillation-First Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is most effective when treated as a flexible, task-aware toolbox rather than a single recipe. Best results arise from (1) transferring internal, structured representations in addition to logits, (2) adapting teacher signals to student capacity and task constraints, and (3) combining distillation with complementary compression strategies such as progressive module replacement or structured pruning. This position synthesizes empirical and algorithmic advances to recommend practical design patterns for building compact, robust models for deployment in vision, language, and reinforcement-learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most usefully viewed not as a single algorithm but as a configurable, task-aware toolbox. When practitioners select what to transfer (logits, hidden states, attention maps, or structured behaviors), adapt teacher signals to student capacity, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, progressive module replacement, or teacher adaptation), KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness constraints. However, KD has limits — it depends on data complexity, teacher–student capacity gaps, and the choice of transferred signals — and in some regimes alternative compression strategies can match or exceed distillation unless hybridized thoughtfully.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Hybrid Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is most effective when treated not as a single recipe but as a task-aware, hybrid toolbox: designers should select which teacher signals to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, attention/feature maps, or training dynamics), adapt teacher supervision to student capacity, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, progressive module replacement, or module-substitution schedules). When these design choices are matched to task constraints and data availability, distilled students can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness requirements. Remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, selecting task-relevant internal signals, and closing large teacher–student capacity gaps without overconstraining the student.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a flexible, task-aware toolbox for producing compact, deployable models. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond simple soft-target matching into a diverse set of approaches that transfer outputs, internal representations, and training dynamics; employ single, multi, or evolving teachers; and combine with complementary compression techniques such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement. Empirical results across vision and natural language tasks show that, when matched to student capacity, task constraints, and data availability, distillation often yields substantial improvements in accuracy, latency, and memory compared to naive shrink-and-fine-tune baselines. Remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness and decision-boundary information, selecting task-relevant intermediate signals, and reducing dependence on large unlabeled corpora or heavy distillation compute.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring useful predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models to smaller students. The field encompasses a wide spectrum of techniques — matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, layer-wise or module replacement, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher strategies, and combinations with structured pruning — each suited to different capacity gaps, data regimes, latency constraints, and robustness needs. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation helps by smoothing supervision, reducing data complexity, shaping per-instance gradients and decision boundaries, and providing representational priors that smaller models can exploit. Effective compression typically requires choosing or adapting what is transferred to the student's capacity and the target task, and often benefits from hybrid strategies (e.g., distillation plus pruning or progressive replacement).

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and How to Use It
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and flexible route to producing compact, high-performance models for deep learning and NLP. When matched to task requirements and student capacity and when combined with complementary compression strategies, distillation routinely yields models that approach the accuracy of large teachers while delivering meaningful latency and memory gains. However, distillation is not universally superior: its benefits depend on what form of knowledge is transferred, the availability and complexity of training data, and the desired properties (e.g., robustness, latency). I argue that distillation should be treated as an indispensable component of a compression toolbox — applied with representation-level signals, teacher-aware adaptations, and hybridization with pruning or progressive replacement when appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical design space for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Methods range from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and feature correlations, and extend to adversarial, contrastive, curriculum, multi-teacher, and meta-learned strategies. Best practices emphasize selecting which teacher signals to transfer, matching distilled information to student capacity and task needs, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement to meet latency, memory, and robustness constraints. Empirical work across vision, language, ranking, and reinforcement learning shows that task-aware, hybrid distillation pipelines typically deliver the most reliable trade-offs between size, speed, and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Complementary Tools and Task-Aware Strategies for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central technique for compressing large neural models into efficient students while preserving performance. A growing literature demonstrates a wide array of KD formulations—response-based, feature-based, layer-wise, adversarial, progressive replacing, and online/evolutionary teacher strategies—each addressing specific limitations such as teacher-student capacity gap, internal representation mismatch, adversarial vulnerability, data complexity, and continual learning. Distillation should be treated as a toolbox: methods must be chosen and combined according to task demands (e.g., NLP summarization, ranking, detection, or incremental learning) and practical constraints (data availability, latency, and robustness requirements). When combined with structured pruning or task-aware layer filtering, distillation can achieve large speedups with small accuracy loss; in some settings simple shrink-and-fine-tune can also be competitive. Overall, effective compression requires matching the distillation technique to the target task and model constraints rather than applying a single off-the-shelf recipe.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation remains a central and practical approach for compressing large deep models into compact, deployable ones. When applied thoughtfully — by distilling internal representations, aligning intermediate layers in a task-aware way, optimizing teacher dynamics, and using distributional or adversarial objectives — distillation can deliver accuracy, latency, and robustness gains across vision, ranking, and NLP tasks. Distillation should be treated not as a single recipe but as a toolkit: combine representation-level transfer, teacher engineering (including learned or evolving teachers), multi-teacher confidence weighting, and targeted adversarial or contrastive objectives. In some settings structured pruning or simple shrink-and-fine-tune strategies are competitive, so practitioners should match the distillation strategy to data availability, task complexity, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods form a broad, task-aware toolbox for turning large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students. The literature spans soft-target (logit) matching, alignment of internal representations and attention, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, self-distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical success typically requires adapting teacher signals to student capacity, selecting which signals to transfer given task constraints, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods when latency, data, or robustness requirements demand it.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring information from a teacher to a smaller student. Methods vary widely: matching output soft-labels, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial and contrastive approaches, curriculum and meta-learning strategies, and task-aware layer selection. In NLP, and particularly with large pretrained Transformers, distillation is applied both during pretraining and fine-tuning; alternative compression strategies (e.g., pruning) are often combined with distillation to trade off size, speed, and accuracy. Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms by which distillation helps students, including regularization, reduced data complexity, and per-instance gradient shaping.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware, Hybrid Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD has diversified beyond simple soft-label matching into a toolbox of methods—representation alignment, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, curriculum- and route-based supervision, and hybrid pipelines that pair distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. When designed to match what is transferred to student capacity and the requirements of the target task, KD enables compact models that retain high accuracy, improved latency, and often better robustness than naïve compression approaches.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring outputs, internal representations, and training dynamics from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label matching to a rich design space that includes intermediate-representation alignment, multi- and online-teacher schemes, self-distillation, adversarial and contrastive objectives, curriculum- and route-based schedules, task-aware layer-wise filtering, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Empirical and analytical work across vision and NLP shows that distillation, when matched to student capacity and task constraints and often combined with complementary compression methods, reliably improves compact-model performance while exposing remaining challenges in robustness, data requirements, and teacher–student mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD's strength derives from a flexible design space — transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention or feature correlations, and decision-boundary information — and from compatibility with complementary strategies such as structured pruning, progressive module replacement, and teacher adaptation. While KD does not universally dominate every setting, when applied in a task-aware, representation-focused, and teacher-aware way it reliably yields compact models that approach teacher performance while delivering practical latency, memory, and robustness benefits.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Across vision and NLP, KD variants transfer information ranging from final soft-labels to intermediate representations, attention maps, and structured feature correlations; practitioners routinely combine distillation with complementary compression methods (e.g., structured pruning or progressive module replacement) and adapt teacher signals to student capacity and task demands. Empirical and theoretical work identifies multiple mechanisms for KD’s effectiveness — better optimization trajectories, regularization-like effects, richer concept learning, and per-instance gradient shaping — while also highlighting important practical factors such as teacher–student capacity gap, the availability of unlabeled data, and robustness transfer. Open problems include reliably selecting task-relevant signals to transfer, minimizing unnecessary constraints from mismatched teachers, and integrating distillation with pruning or architectural changes to maximize latency and accuracy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad and practically central approach for producing compact neural models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. Research over the past decade has expanded KD from simple soft-label matching to a diverse toolkit that includes internal-representation alignment, adversarial and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher schedules, student-friendly teacher training, and hybrid pipelines combining distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals and teacher strategies to student capacity, task requirements, and available data; when designed carefully, KD enables substantial latency and memory gains while retaining strong accuracy across vision, NLP, ranking, retrieval, and reinforcement-learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from training compact students on teacher soft labels to a diverse set of techniques that transfer knowledge via logits, intermediate representations, attention, adversarial objectives, and dynamic teacher-student interactions. Modern work emphasizes transferring internal structure (e.g., feature maps, layer representations, inter-channel correlations), leveraging multiple or evolving teachers, and combining distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement for efficient deployment. Applications range from machine translation and summarization to ranking, detection, reinforcement learning, and robustness, and recent advances show task-aware, confidence-weighted, and adversarial approaches often outperform vanilla logit-matching.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach for producing compact, deployable models in deep learning and NLP. Its power arises from multiple distinct mechanisms of transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/feature maps, and training dynamics) and from the flexibility to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (structured pruning, progressive module replacement, adversarial objectives, and curriculum schedules). KD is not a universal panacea: its success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, adapting teacher signals over training, and considering data, latency, and robustness constraints. Best practice treats KD as a hybrid, task-aware toolbox whose components are chosen and combined to meet the target application’s constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used family of techniques that compress large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. KD has evolved from soft-label matching into many variants—intermediate-representation alignment, contrastive and adversarial objectives, curriculum and route-based supervision, online/multi-teacher strategies, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or module replacement. Practical success depends on matching the type of transferred signal to student capacity and task demands, adapting teacher signals during training, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques to meet latency, memory, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and its Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning based models are relatively large, and it is hard to deploy such models on resource-limited devices such as mobile phones and embedded devices. One possible solution is knowledge distillation whereby a smaller model (student model) is trained by utilizing the information from a larger model (teacher model). In this paper, we present a survey of knowledge distillation techniques applied to deep learning models. To compare the performances of different techniques, we propose a new metric called distillation metric. Distillation metric compares different knowledge distillation algorithms based on sizes and accuracy scores. Based on the survey, some interesting conclusions are drawn and presented in this paper.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and How to Use It
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and flexible route to producing compact, high-performance models for deep learning and NLP. When matched to task requirements and student capacity and when combined with complementary compression strategies, distillation routinely yields models that approach the accuracy of large teachers while delivering meaningful latency and memory gains. However, distillation is not universally superior: its benefits depend on what form of knowledge is transferred, the availability and complexity of training data, and the desired properties (e.g., robustness, latency). I argue that distillation should be treated as an indispensable component of a compression toolbox — applied with representation-level signals, teacher-aware adaptations, and hybridization with pruning or progressive replacement when appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Best Practices (Synthesis)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller students. Over the last decade KD diversified from simple soft-label transfer into many variants that match logits, internal representations, attention/feature maps, or training dynamics, and that interact with complementary compression tools such as structured pruning and progressive module replacement. Practical deployment benefits most from hybrid, task-aware strategies that select what to transfer, adapt the teacher-student relationship, and combine distillation with pruning or architectural replacement to meet latency, memory, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware, Hybrid Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD has diversified beyond simple soft-label matching into a toolbox of methods—representation alignment, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, curriculum- and route-based supervision, and hybrid pipelines that pair distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. When designed to match what is transferred to student capacity and the requirements of the target task, KD enables compact models that retain high accuracy, improved latency, and often better robustness than naïve compression approaches.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Exploring Inter-Channel Correlation for Diversity-preserved KnowledgeDistillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation has shown very promising abil-ity in transferring learned representation from the largermodel (teacher) to the smaller one (student).Despitemany efforts, prior methods ignore the important role ofretaining inter-channel correlation of features, leading tothe lack of capturing intrinsic distribution of the featurespace and sufficient diversity properties of features in theteacher network.To solve the issue, we propose thenovel Inter-Channel Correlation for Knowledge Distillation(ICKD), with which the diversity and homology of the fea-ture space of the student network can align with that ofthe teacher network. The correlation between these twochannels is interpreted as diversity if they are irrelevantto each other, otherwise homology. Then the student isrequired to mimic the correlation within its own embed-ding space. In addition, we introduce the grid-level inter-channel correlation, making it capable of dense predictiontasks. Extensive experiments on two vision tasks, includ-ing ImageNet classification and Pascal VOC segmentation,demonstrate the superiority of our ICKD, which consis-tently outperforms many existing methods, advancing thestate-of-the-art in the fields of Knowledge Distillation. Toour knowledge, we are the first method based on knowl-edge distillation boosts ResNet18 beyond 72% Top-1 ac-curacy on ImageNet classification. Code is available at:https://github.com/ADLab-AutoDrive/ICKD.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques constitute a broad design space for transferring predictive behavior from large teacher models to smaller, deployable students. Methods range from soft-target matching to internal-representation alignment, progressive module replacement, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or task-aware filtering. Empirical evidence across natural language tasks (classification, summarization, translation, retrieval) and other domains shows that KD can preserve or approach teacher performance while improving latency and memory, but its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, data complexity, and task constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Complementary Tools and Task-Aware Strategies for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central technique for compressing large neural models into efficient students while preserving performance. A growing literature demonstrates a wide array of KD formulations—response-based, feature-based, layer-wise, adversarial, progressive replacing, and online/evolutionary teacher strategies—each addressing specific limitations such as teacher-student capacity gap, internal representation mismatch, adversarial vulnerability, data complexity, and continual learning. Distillation should be treated as a toolbox: methods must be chosen and combined according to task demands (e.g., NLP summarization, ranking, detection, or incremental learning) and practical constraints (data availability, latency, and robustness requirements). When combined with structured pruning or task-aware layer filtering, distillation can achieve large speedups with small accuracy loss; in some settings simple shrink-and-fine-tune can also be competitive. Overall, effective compression requires matching the distillation technique to the target task and model constraints rather than applying a single off-the-shelf recipe.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Across vision and NLP, KD variants transfer information ranging from final soft-labels to intermediate representations, attention maps, and structured feature correlations; practitioners routinely combine distillation with complementary compression methods (e.g., structured pruning or progressive module replacement) and adapt teacher signals to student capacity and task demands. Empirical and theoretical work identifies multiple mechanisms for KD’s effectiveness — better optimization trajectories, regularization-like effects, richer concept learning, and per-instance gradient shaping — while also highlighting important practical factors such as teacher–student capacity gap, the availability of unlabeled data, and robustness transfer. Open problems include reliably selecting task-relevant signals to transfer, minimizing unnecessary constraints from mismatched teachers, and integrating distillation with pruning or architectural changes to maximize latency and accuracy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible set of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task awareness — selecting what to transfer, adapting teacher signals to student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques — distillation routinely yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness constraints. Practical success depends on careful design choices (what to match, how to adapt teachers, and whether to incorporate pruning or progressive replacement) rather than a single canonical recipe.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring useful predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models to smaller students. The field encompasses a wide spectrum of techniques — matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, layer-wise or module replacement, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher strategies, and combinations with structured pruning — each suited to different capacity gaps, data regimes, latency constraints, and robustness needs. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation helps by smoothing supervision, reducing data complexity, shaping per-instance gradients and decision boundaries, and providing representational priors that smaller models can exploit. Effective compression typically requires choosing or adapting what is transferred to the student's capacity and the target task, and often benefits from hybrid strategies (e.g., distillation plus pruning or progressive replacement).

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Its strengths arise from multiple complementary mechanisms (soft targets, internal representation transfer, teacher engineering, and supervised schedules), and the most reliable practical strategies treat KD as a configurable toolbox that is combined with pruning or module replacement when deployment constraints demand it. Practitioners obtain the best trade-offs by matching distilled signals to student capacity, adapting teacher dynamics to the task, and using hybrid pipelines tailored to data, latency, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes the state of knowledge distillation (KD) and its role in model compression for deep learning and NLP. It surveys what is transferred from teachers to students (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/feature correlations, and training dynamics), how teachers and students are coupled (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and progressive/evolving schemes), the principal mechanisms by which distillation benefits students (label smoothing, reduced data complexity, representation shaping, and gradient/decision-boundary effects), common applications across NLP tasks, empirical practicalities and trade-offs (teacher–student capacity gap, data requirements, robustness transfer, and compute/latency constraints), and recommended task-aware, hybrid practices that combine distillation with pruning or module replacement. The synthesis also highlights recurring open challenges such as reliably transferring robustness, selecting task-relevant teacher signals for a given student capacity, and reducing dependence on large unlabeled corpora.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Hybrid Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Rather than a single recipe, effective distillation is a design space of complementary techniques — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, adversarial/contrastive objectives, multi- or evolving-teacher schedules, student-friendly teacher design, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or progressive module replacement. When chosen and combined with attention to teacher–student capacity, task characteristics, and data availability, distillation reliably yields compact models that preserve accuracy and can transfer robustness; when misapplied it can be outperformed by simpler shrink-and-fine-tune or structured pruning strategies. I argue that the best practical posture is to treat distillation as a task-aware hybrid toolbox: prioritize representation-level transfer and teacher engineering, use confidence- or task-aware weighting for multiple signals, integrate robustness-aware objectives when needed, and combine distillation with pruning or module replacement when latency/memory constraints dominate.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Task-Aware Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger models (teachers) into smaller models (students) to achieve deployable efficiency. The literature has expanded from simple soft-label matching to a broad toolbox that includes logits and intermediate-representation transfer, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, progressive module replacement, and hybrid pipelines combining distillation with pruning or module replacement. Empirical and analytic work shows that effectiveness depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, the target task, and available data; combining complementary compression tools often yields the best practical trade-offs. Open challenges include the teacher–student capacity gap, reliable transfer of robustness, and minimizing dependence on large unlabeled corpora.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a rich set of methods to transfer information from larger "teacher" models to smaller "student" models or to produce compact models via pruning and module replacement. Approaches vary from matching soft targets to aligning internal representations, using adversarial objectives, contrastive or Wasserstein-based objectives, layer-wise and task-aware filters, and online or evolutionary teacher schedules. These techniques have been applied across domains including natural language understanding, summarization, machine translation, ranking, vision tasks, reinforcement learning, and incremental learning. Empirical work highlights that the benefits of distillation depend on teacher-student capacity gaps, what kind of knowledge is transferred (global label structure, domain priors, instance-specific signals), and data complexity; combining distillation with structured pruning or careful teacher selection often yields practical gains in latency and storage while preserving accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring functional behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD evolved from soft-target supervision into a rich toolbox that includes internal-representation alignment, attention/feature matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schemes, confidence- and task-aware weighting, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with structured pruning or progressive module replacement. Effective compression is task- and constraint-aware: the best choices depend on what signals are transferred, how teachers are constructed or adapted, student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints (latency, memory, and robustness). While KD often yields strong accuracy–latency trade-offs across vision and NLP tasks, remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, reducing heavy distillation data or compute needs, and selecting task-relevant intermediate signals.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, language, and reinforcement learning shows that success depends less on a single canonical loss and more on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and adapted to the student and the target task. Best results arise when distillation methods (1) expose informative internal representations rather than only final logits, (2) adapt or curate teacher signals to match student capacity and task needs, and (3) combine distillation with complementary compression strategies (e.g., structured pruning or progressive module replacement). When applied with attention to these aspects, distillation yields compact models that maintain high accuracy, can inherit robustness, and scale to practical inference budgets.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across vision and NLP. The literature provides many complementary distillation objectives and workflows — soft-label transfer, intermediate-representation matching, adversarial/contrastive losses, online and multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Effectiveness depends strongly on teacher–student capacity gaps, the exact form of transferred information, task characteristics, and data availability; best practice is to select or adapt distillation signals to the student and downstream task and to combine methods where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from soft-label transfer into a broad, task-aware toolkit for producing compact models in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student performance by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, and training dynamics, but its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, task demands, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as part of a hybrid compression pipeline—selecting what to transfer, adapting teacher signals, and combining distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement when needed.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher. The literature expands beyond simple soft-label matching to include internal-representation matching, layer-wise and task-aware filters, adversarial and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, meta-learned teachers, and complementary pruning strategies. Applications span NLP (BERT compression, machine translation, non-autoregressive translation, summarization, dense retrieval), vision (classification, detection, pose regression), reinforcement learning, and continual learning. Key practical concerns include the teacher–student capacity gap, selection or weighting of teacher signals, reliance on unlabeled data, robustness, and efficient architectural shrinking. Empirical and theoretical work characterizes what is transferred (from label-smoothing-like regularization to instance-specific gradient rescaling and internal concept representations) and proposes methods to better align student representations with useful teacher knowledge. Open directions include task-aware selection of representational targets, minimizing unnecessary constraints from converged teachers, and combining structured pruning with targeted distillation to maximize latency and accuracy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a flexible, task-aware toolbox for producing compact, deployable models. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond simple soft-target matching into a diverse set of approaches that transfer outputs, internal representations, and training dynamics; employ single, multi, or evolving teachers; and combine with complementary compression techniques such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement. Empirical results across vision and natural language tasks show that, when matched to student capacity, task constraints, and data availability, distillation often yields substantial improvements in accuracy, latency, and memory compared to naive shrink-and-fine-tune baselines. Remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness and decision-boundary information, selecting task-relevant intermediate signals, and reducing dependence on large unlabeled corpora or heavy distillation compute.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a versatile and effective approach for compressing large models into compact, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD’s strengths arise from its ability to transfer soft targets, internal representations, and task-relevant signals to reshape student training dynamics, and it admits many practical variants (multi-teacher, adversarial, curriculum, online/evolutionary, and progressive replacement). At the same time, structured pruning and module-replacement methods can be competitive or complementary when latency, data, or compute constraints dominate. Best practice is a toolbox mentality: choose what to transfer to match student capacity, adapt the teacher–student relationship during training, and combine distillation with pruning or curriculum strategies when appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from simple soft-label transfer into a broad, task-aware toolbox of methods for producing compact, deployable models. Contemporary KD techniques include matching logits, aligning internal representations or attention maps, adversarial and contrastive objectives, self- and online-distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Empirical work across vision, language, and reinforcement learning shows that no single KD recipe dominates all settings: effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher–student capacity gaps, task complexity, and data availability. Practical compression typically requires selecting or adapting distilled signals to student capacity and combining complementary methods to meet latency, memory, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible, task-aware toolbox and combined with complementary techniques (structured pruning, progressive module replacement, confidence weighting, and teacher adaptation), distillation routinely delivers favorable accuracy–latency trade-offs. However, its effectiveness depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing teacher–student gaps, considering data and compute constraints, and explicitly accounting for robustness requirements.
